page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.small is an entry-level shared instance within the ecs.n4 server family. Built on KVM virtualization and x86_64 architecture, it features a single physical Intel Xeon 8269CY core running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The allocation provides 1 vCPU without multithreading enabled. The system includes 2.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core, backed by 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. Architectural capabilities include hardware acceleration flags for AVX, AVX-512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AES cryptography. The configuration does not include local disk storage, dedicated baseline network bandwidth, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate entry-level baseline performance across computational and memory operations. Single-threaded stress-ng and PassMark CPU metrics score 1061.69 and 1277.65 respectively, positioning CPU throughput in lower baseline ranges. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 8.61 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measures 7.28 GB/sec. Operational benchmarks demonstrate 1.22 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.22 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Inferencing with a small 135M parameter LLM yields 128.79 tokens per second for prompt processing and 38.66 tokens per second for text generation.

The shared vCPU model offers low hardware density suited for cost-sensitive environments where continuous maximum CPU utilization is unnecessary. Key trade-offs involve potential resource contention from shared CPU allocation and the absence of bundled local NVMe storage or dedicated baseline network throughput. Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.small is appropriate for light development, staging environments, basic background tasks, non-critical microservices, and low-traffic web serving.
